props.gloss_en: in R' Yosei HaGelili's name they said: nor may women's bills of divorce be written on it (on the living thing of the earlier baraita -- the antecedent is Steinsaltz's rendering)
the baraita: 'scroll' -- I have only a scroll; whence to include every object? the verse says 'and he shall write her', in any manner
the baraita: if so, why does it say 'scroll'? to tell you: as a scroll is a thing without life and not food, so any thing without life and not food
the Rabbis: had it written 'in the scroll', it would be as you say; now that it writes 'scroll', it comes merely for an account of matters
the Rabbis use 'and he shall write' for: she is divorced by writing, and is not divorced by money
R' Yosei HaGelili derives it from 'a scroll of severance': a scroll severs her, and nothing else severs her
the Rabbis need 'scroll of severance' for: [the get must be] a thing that severs between him and her
the baraita: 'here is your get on condition that you never drink wine / never go to your father's house' -- that is not severance; 'for thirty days' -- that is severance
R' Yosei HaGelili derives [the severing-thing requirement] from 'karet' written as 'keritut'
